experiments.primary_claim: Distinguish control defects and nondeterminism from state-dependent contact failures.
Find physically useful, executable contact-phase corrections under full-task constraints.
Get well-trained same-authority residual RL, with full-cost baselines.
Isolate additional causal value of explicit action-effect feedback over equal-observation/history RL and strong planning.
After a reliable independent gain, test novel conditions, another contact mechanism and industrial adapter.

unresolved_questions: Do legitimate new grasp/attachment/task/contact conditions expose repeatable failure of the best depth-hold+replan controller?
Are different legal actions beneficial under different current observations or short action-effect probes, rather than one always-best rule?
Can physically plausible unobserved dynamics/contact changes generate state aliasing that effect history helps resolve beyond generic history and strong online adaptive control?
Can mature residual PPO/SAC trained on enough genuine effective decisions improve full-task success, and does any new mechanism beat matched baselines?
